thread:
Alice Martin: FYI - AcmeLib reported a ~60% drop in vectors/sec on /v1/embeddings yesterday evening, tokens/sec for text endpoints unaffected. customer says latency spikes and occasional 429s for large bursts.
Ben Cho: do we have customer id + sample payload? can we repro in staging?
Alice Martin: AcmeOrg (acct: ACME-773). They sent ~120k requests/min, mostly 1-3 vectors per request after a client-side change. Sample curl attached.
Alice Martin: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["short sentence"]}'
Chloe Rivera: pulled the Grafana panels - saw GPU queue_depth spike when vectors/sec dropped. tokens/sec steady. panels: embeddings_p95_latency, gpu_queue_depth, batch_window_ms, batch_sizes_percentile.
Chloe Rivera: snippet: 
```
time=2026-03-12T19:04:12Z gpu_queue_depth=24 batch_window_ms=12 avg_batch_size=2.1 vectors/sec=4500 -> baseline 12000
```
Dmitri Petrov: low avg_batch_size + high queue depth = thundering tiny-batch problem. autoscaler didn't spin up more slots because CPU dims looked ok.
Ben Cho: any recent rollouts touching batching/autoscale or quant profile?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout completed: autoscale-policy v2.3 -> v2.4 to embeddings-service at 2026-03-12T18:50:03Z (config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10, batch_window_ms default changed from 8->12)
Chloe Rivera: ah that change lines up. bumping batch_window_ms reduced overhead for large tokens flows but for small many-small-requests it increases number of micro-batches queued and GPU slot contention.
Alice Martin: customer observed auth/billing errors too but our logs show 200/429 mix. Looks like some 429s from service-side rate limiting when queue depth overflowed. no 401s.
Dmitri Petrov: hypothesis: client shift to 1-3 vectors/req increased request rate, batch_window_ms increase to 12ms caused more partial batches hitting GPUs, amortized kernel launch overhead went up and GPU occupancy dropped -> vectors/sec down. plus autoscaler thresholds based on cpu/latency didn't trigger because p95 latency jittered within threshold.
Ben Cho: can we get a quick repro in staging by replaying APM traffic? scale down to embed-large-v2 and replay at same qps with 1-3 per req. I'll run loadgen.
Chloe Rivera: reproducer steps: 1) deploy embed service with autoscale-policy v2.4 2) run loadgen with 120k rps/m burst pattern 3) sample metrics: gpu_queue_depth, avg_batch_size, kernel_util. attach script below.
Chloe Rivera: ./scripts/emb-load.sh --model embed-large-v2 --qps 2000 --concurrency 500 --payload-size 1-3
Dmitri Petrov: quick mitigation options for customer: 1) revert batch_window_ms to 8ms for shared pool 2) enable small-batch aggregation optimization (internal flag: EMBED_SMALL_BATCH_HANDOFF=true) 3) route AcmeOrg to dedicated pool with min_replicas=4 until client fixes chunking.
Alice Martin: i applied EMBED_SMALL_BATCH_HANDOFF=true for AcmeOrg rule and bumped their route to dedicated-pool-preview, monitoring now.
infra-bot: autoscaler: new replica count for embeddings-service -> 6 replicas (scale up triggered by queue_depth policy)
Chloe Rivera: after tweak, avg_batch_size -> 4.8, gpu_queue_depth down to 6, vectors/sec climbing back toward baseline.
Alice Martin: customer reports improved latency and fewer 429s. they're rolling a client-side fix to batch at 16 vectors/req.
Ben Cho: followups: - create a runbook entry for small-request thundering herd on embeddings - add an alert on (gpu_queue_depth>20 && avg_batch_size<3) - consider making batch_window_ms adaptive by request-size distribution.
Dmitri Petrov: i'll open a PR to add adaptive-window experiment and add a canary gate to autoscale policy.
Alice Martin: leaving notes for support handoff: customer acct ACME-773 routed to dedicated preview, EMBED_SMALL_BATCH_HANDOFF=true applied, monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/dev/d/embeds/acme-773, contact: acme-eng@acme.com.
Ben Cho: thanks team. marking resolved for now but keep channel open for 24h to confirm stability. :thumbsup:
Alice Martin: thanks all. :party:
